title: 2.2.11 Collectible Class
description: Write a Collectible class, instantiate at least 5, and detect overlap with the player. SLO-2 lab — the class is the point. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Define the Collectible class
steps.instructions: Write `class Collectible { }` with a `constructor(x, y, value, color)`. Store the data on `this` and create `this.sprite = new Sprite(...)`.
hints: Re-read 2.2.8 Worked Example — the `Enemy` constructor follows the same `this.x = x` / `this.sprite = new Sprite(...)` pattern.

steps.title: Add a collect() method
steps.instructions: Add a `collect()` method on the class that despawns the sprite and returns `this.value`.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the q5play docs drawer for how to despawn a sprite.

steps.title: Instantiate at least 5 Collectibles
steps.instructions: In `setup()` (after the player is created), push at least 5 `new Collectible(...)` into the `collectibles` array at different positions, with different values and colors.
hints: A `for` loop with `collectibles.push(new Collectible(...))` is one option — a `const` per item works too.

steps.title: Detect overlaps and collect
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, iterate the `collectibles` array. When the player overlaps a collectible's sprite, call its `collect()` method, add the returned value to `totalScore`, and remove that item from the array.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the q5play docs drawer for the overlap check.
Removing items while iterating forwards skips neighbours — search for 'iterate backwards to splice' if you hit that bug.

requirements.title: collect() method
requirements.description: A collect method exists in the class.

requirements.title: At least one instance
requirements.description: At least one Collectible is instantiated.

requirements.title: Overlap detection
requirements.description: The code checks for overlap between player and a sprite.
